html:
The constitution of Mexico, written in 1917 in Querétaro during the Mexican Revolution and still in force today, though amended many times. It was one of the first constitutions in the world to promise social rights as well as political ones.

The convention was called by the revolutionary leader Venustiano Carranza, but more radical delegates pushed it further than he wanted. Its best-known articles:

  • Article 3: free, secular public schooling.
  • Article 27: land, water and what lies under the ground belong to the nation. This allowed land reform through village lands called ejidos, and later the takeover of foreign oil companies in 1938.
  • Article 123: workers' rights, including the eight-hour day, a minimum wage and the right to strike.
  • Article 130: tight limits on the Catholic Church.

The rules against the church led to the Cristero War of 1926 to 1929. The constitution came before the Soviet constitution of 1918 and Germany's Weimar constitution of 1919, and it influenced later constitutions in Latin America.
